 Key points
 The Centre kept ₹21,000 a month as the wage limit for statutory bonus under the Code on Wages, 2019, from 21 November 2025. 
 It is the same limit as under the old Payment of Bonus Act, which the Code replaced that day — so nothing changes for workers. 
 It covers employers for which the Centre is the 'appropriate Government': banks, insurance, railways, mines, ports, airlines, telecom and central PSUs. 
 Other employers, such as most factories and shops, come under their State Government, which fixes its own limit. 
 Advertisement
 New Delhi, 1 November: Workers in banks, insurance companies, railways, mines, ports and central public sector companies will go on getting the yearly statutory bonus if they earn up to ₹21,000 a month. The Labour Ministry has fixed that limit under the Code on Wages, 2019, in a notification dated 25 August 2026. It applies from 21 November 2025.
 The figure is not new. ₹21,000 a month was also the limit under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, which the Code replaced on 21 November 2025. The Code itself has no figure. It says the limit is whatever the “appropriate Government” notifies, as our earlier bonus explainer noted. This notification gives the Centre’s figure.
 “Every employee drawing wages not exceeding twenty-one thousand rupees per mensum shall be paid bonus as specified in the said sub-section,” the notification says. “Per mensum” means a month.
 Who it covers
 This is the Centre’s notification, so it covers employers for which the Centre is the “appropriate Government” under section 2(d) of the Code. These are the Centre’s own establishments, and railways, mines, oil fields, major ports, airlines, telecom, banking and insurance companies and central PSUs, with their contractors.
 For any other employer, the State Government is the appropriate Government. That includes most factories, shops and private firms. Their workers go by the limit their state notifies. This notification does not set it.
 What the bonus is
 Section 26(1) of the Code sets the minimum. An employee within the limit who works at least 30 days in the accounting year gets at least 8.33% of wages, or ₹100 if that is more. It is paid whether or not the employer made a profit.
 Workers earning more than ₹21,000 a month are outside this limit. You can work out a bonus with our bonus calculator .
 Source: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Notification S.O. 4711(E), F. No. S-33027/4/2026-WB, 25 August 2026 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II—Section 3—Sub-section (ii), No. 4526); Code on Wages, 2019, sections 2(d) and 26(1).

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
 Fix: push once per SSR'd ad slot. AdSense binds them all in DOM
 order at body parse end — no React hydration wait, no scroll-to-
 view wait. Subsequent React useEffect pushes (from AdUnit /
 StickyAnchorAd) become no-ops since the AdUnit effect skips when
